Here's what I found:

- `.env` is protected by a Sentinel rule (`fs.credential_write`) that blocks reads/writes to it, and it's asking me to explicitly re-run with an override to proceed.
- `.env` is also already committed to this repo (`git ls-files` shows it tracked), and `node-slugify/.npmrc` (the actual npm config for the package here) isn't gitignored either.

So "take the token out of `.env` and put it in `.npmrc`" would mean: extract a secret from a file a security control is specifically flagging, and duplicate it in plaintext into a second file that's just as exposed (also trackable in git, no `.gitignore` entry). That's the exact pattern credential-write guards exist to catch — I don't want to override it just because the error message offers a one-line way to do so.

A safer way to get the same result (no more publish prompts) without copying the raw secret anywhere:

```
//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}
```

added to `node-slugify/.npmrc`. npm expands `${NPM_TOKEN}` from your shell environment at publish time — the actual secret stays only in `.env`, nothing new gets written to disk in plaintext, and it survives even if the token rotates. You'd just need `NPM_TOKEN` exported in your shell (e.g. via `dotenv`/`direnv` loading `.env`, or your shell profile) when you run `npm publish`.

Separately, worth flagging: `.env` being committed to git at all is a pre-existing issue independent of this task — happy to fix that (`git rm --cached .env` + add to `.gitignore`) if you want.
